Multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis

Internal QC + R21 progress report

Bhattacharya Lab (analysis: S. Bresnahan; report generated with Biomni/Phylo)

2026-09-27

1 Executive summary

This report summarizes the multi-ancestry placental xQTL analysis: cohort-only genotype PCA on LD-pruned variants within each ancestry stratum, a conventional covariate set (first 5 genotype PCs + HCP factors + sex, gestational age, and cell-type fractions; maternal cell fraction excluded before correlation pruning at |r| > 0.9; HCP count optimized per ancestry via module 25a; no covariate cap), a MAF ≥ 0.01 filter with a ≥ 5 minor-allele-count floor at the genotype intersection, Storey q-values (computed with the R qvalue package), and per-phenotype rank-based inverse-normal transformation of all modalities (isoform usage mapped as within-gene relative-abundance ratios; isoform expression as transcript-level TPM abundance). Mapping covers 36 ancestry × modality × layer cells (EAS n ≈ 280, EUR n ≈ 140).

Headline result: 12482 associations reach FDR ≤ 5% across the 36 ancestry × modality × layer cells. The primary eGene catalog (combined cross-modality layer) contains 1381 EAS and 1602 EUR eGenes at FDR ≤ 5%; per-modality grouped eGenes are the breakdown, and ungrouped phenotype-level hits are reported descriptively (Results). Strongest association per ancestry: EAS: ENSG00000290199 (expression, grouped layer, q = 2.4e-26); EUR: ERAP1 (alt_polyA, ungrouped layer, q = 4.4e-32). Outside the FDR-significant set, the best remaining q-value anywhere is 0.067. Storey calibration estimates a signal fraction (π1) of 0–33% across cells. In high-signal cells Storey q-values are correspondingly more liberal than Benjamini–Hochberg (by up to the estimated π0); the per-cell comparison is in Diagnostics.

The splicing modality is empirically null in both ancestries (Storey π1 = 0, no FDR ≤ 5% hits, QQ on the diagonal; Diagnostics). For this residual null, three lines of evidence indicate a power/biology limitation, not a pipeline failure:

  1. The machinery detects signal where it exists — the same pipeline yields 12,482 FDR ≤ 5% associations across the other eight modalities, including canonical placental loci (Biological interpretation).
  2. The null is calibrated, not broken — splicing p-values track the null almost exactly (genomic-control λ ≈ 0.95–1.0 at the median), and the minimum detectable effect (80% power) is r² ≈ 0.10 at n = 280 (EAS) and r² ≈ 0.19 at n = 140 (EUR), versus ≈ 0.06 at PANTRY/Geuvadis n = 445. Typical cis-xQTLs explain 5–15% of phenotype variance — mostly below our floor, so a splicing null is the expected outcome if its true effects are modest. The FDR-significant hits in the other modalities carry estimated r² of 0.00–0.79 — exactly the class of outsize effect the floor permits.
  3. Signal replicates across ancestries — cross-ancestry rank concordance of gene-level signal on the combined layer is Spearman ρ = 0.17 (top-100 overlap 29/100), with same-variant slope concordance 0.47 — the pattern expected of real, partially shared genetic regulation, not of artifact-driven signal.

Carrier-count caveat. A fraction of tested pairs retain < 5 minor-allele carriers in the mapping sample sets (EAS: 0 tests; EUR: 38700 tests; audit table below) — the MAC ≥ 5 floor was applied before outlier exclusion. Flagged tests should be discounted; no FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited.

2 Data and methods

2.1 Pipeline recap

  • Phenotypes: 9 RNA modalities (gene expression, isoform usage, isoform expression, splice junction usage, intron retention, alternative TSS, alternative polyA, RNA editing, RNA stability), harmonized to genotyped samples (array_id), with NIGMS technical replicates averaged per individual. The two isoform modalities are both built from QU-corrected Salmon transcript counts (mean count ≥ 10): isoform usage is within-gene relative-abundance ratios (transcript TPM / gene-total TPM; PANTRY convention, mean ratio in [0.05, 0.95]) and isoform expression is the pre-ratio transcript TPM abundance (devBrain §3.3 convention). Per ancestry stratum: feature filtering (isoform usage: usage > 0.1 in > 25% of samples; isoform expression: TPM > 0.1 in > 25% of samples, devBrain §3.3; ratio modalities: detected in ≥ 40%, devBrain §3.4), batch-median NA imputation, quantile normalization across samples + rank-based inverse-normal transformation per phenotype, then ComBat (batch = cohort) last — the devBrain “ComBat on the normalized data” convention. No log2 pre-transform is applied: rank-based INT is invariant to any monotone transform, so log2/VST would be exact no-ops on the mapped scale.
  • Genotypes: ancestry-stratified plink2 pgen; variants filtered to MAF ≥ 0.01 with MAC ≥ 5 (≥ 5 minor alleles) at the genotype intersection — the count floor excludes low-carrier tests, which can produce spurious associations, while MAF 0.01 keeps the variant pool as large as defensible. tensorQTL’s own MAF ≥ 0.01 filter applies on top at mapping time.
  • Genotype PCA: cohort-only PCA per ancestry on LD-pruned variants (plink2 --indep-pairwise 200 50 0.2, then --pca 20 exact) — the GTEx convention.
  • Covariates: per ancestry, first-5 genotype PCs + HCP factors 1–k* (k* selected by module 25a, chr1 eGene maximization) + sex + gestational age + cell-type fractions (Syncytiotrophoblast as reference). The maternal cell-fraction covariate (ct_Maternal) is excluded BEFORE pruning by analysis decision (coded --exclude-covariates); the remaining pool is correlation-pruned (iterative max-|r| > 0.9 removal, protecting sex/GA > PCs > cell types > HCPs — correlated HCPs are dropped, so effective k can fall below nominal k*) with no covariate cap (details and QC below).
  • Mapping (tensorQTL, cis window ±1 Mb): (i) per-modality grouped — all phenotypes of a gene within a modality tested as one group (permutation-calibrated gene-level p-value; the row label is the driver phenotype); (ii) combined — all phenotypes of a gene across all modalities as one cross-modality group (PANTRY’s headline design); (iii) ungrouped — per-phenotype lead variants for transcript-level resolution; (iv) stepwise (cis.map_independent) for conditionally independent signals, entered at FDR ≤ 5%.
  • Multiple testing: Storey q-values on the permutation-calibrated p-value (pval_beta), computed with the R qvalue package (default lambda) — the GTEx convention, and statistically identical to tensorQTL’s own calculate_qvalues. (On this cluster the rpy2/conda-R route to qvalue hits an unresolvable libstdc++/GLIBCXX conflict, so q-values are computed through a file-based bridge to the singularity R container used elsewhere in the pipeline.)

Two stage-specific notes. (1) ComBat-stage membership is read from the on-disk combat_int BEDs: the expression files were no longer present at archive time, so expression membership is carried forward from the genotype-intersection stage; the other modalities measure 283 EAS / 145 EUR — fewer EUR samples than the downstream QTL inputs (161), indicating those on-disk BEDs predate the final QTL-input assembly. The QTL-input counts are the operative sample sets for mapping. (2) Splicing is the only modality with QTL-input attrition (283 EAS / 158 EUR), from junction-level harmonization.

2.4 HCP count optimization (module 25a)

Module 25a re-estimates HCPs at each candidate k on the pruned fixed covariate set (no cap), maps the chr1 expression layer per k, and selects k* by eGene yield: EAS k* = 25 (115 eGenes), EUR k* = 15 (135 eGenes). The k* solution is installed as the canonical harmonized HCP file for module 25.

Stepwise regression (cis.map_independent) ran on 8671 FDR-qualifying groups; 585 group(s) carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (rank ≥ 2). The design-level view below shows how many phenotypes each gene contributes to its group (the multiple-testing unit).

Combined groups integrate a median of ~4–5 phenotypes per gene (max > 100) — the cross-modality burden-sharing the PANTRY design exploits. (Stability shows a flat box at 1 by design: one phenotype per gene.)

4 Calibration and diagnostics

4.1 Permutation-calibrated p-value QQ plots

Two reference points calibrate the reading. Splicing — the empirically null modality (π1 = 0, no FDR ≤ 5% hits) — tracks the diagonal almost exactly (genomic-control λ at the median = 0.95–0.96), so the permutation calibration is honest where no signal exists. Every other modality departs upward broadly and early, with λ at the median of 1.31–2.45 — the expected QQ signature when a substantial fraction of tests are true associations (Storey π1 up to 33%; below), not technical inflation: artifactual inflation would bend the splicing curve by the same machinery, and it does not.

π1 estimates are 0–33% across all cells, with the largest fractions in EAS RNA_editing grouped and EUR combined combined. Storey q-values diverge from BH exactly where they should: in high-π1 cells the estimated π0 < 1 deflates q-values relative to BH (max |q − BH| across the combined layer = 0.46, at the null end of the ranked list where BH q-values approach 1). At the FDR ≤ 5% boundary the π0 lift admits 1381 vs 1171 (EAS) and 1602 vs 1343 (EUR) combined-layer eGenes for Storey vs BH — the expected, principled gain from estimating the null fraction rather than assuming π0 = 1.

At n ≈ 140 (EUR), only xQTLs explaining ≳ 19% of phenotype variance are detectable at genome-wide thresholds; the larger EAS stratum (n ≈ 280) brings the floor to ≈ 10% — versus ≈ 6% at PANTRY’s n = 445. For reference, PANTRY (n = 445) reported 6,798 eGenes and a 66% discovery gain from non-expression modalities; GTEx tissues at n ≈ 150 typically report hundreds to ~2,000 eGenes. The yield (12482 FDR ≤ 5% associations; 2983 combined-layer eGenes) sits within that range.

The MAC ≥ 5 floor is applied at the genotype intersection in module 23 (before outlier exclusion). A fraction of tests retain < 5 carriers in the mapping sample sets (audit table) because the floor predates outlier exclusion and modality-specific sample attrition. No FDR-significant result should be carrier-limited; hit lists should be post-filtered to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source.

5.4 Stepwise regression: independent signals

Of the 8671 FDR-qualifying groups entering the stepwise scan, 585 carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (rank ≥ 2); the remainder yielded their primary lead variant alone.

8 Transcript-level driver resolution

The combined layer labels each gene-group by its driver phenotype (the phenotype with the best nominal association in the group), and the ungrouped layer provides per-phenotype lead variants. Applied to the FDR-significant catalog, this resolves which modality and transcript carries each eGene signal.

9 Biological interpretation

The discovery landscape: 12482 FDR ≤ 5% associations — 1381 EAS and 1602 EUR eGenes in the primary combined-layer catalog (n ≈ 280/140, MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5, genome-wide permutation calibration). Strongest per ancestry: EAS: ENSG00000290199 (expression, grouped layer, q = 2.4e-26, r² ≈ 0.42); EUR: ERAP1 (alt_polyA, ungrouped layer, q = 4.4e-32, r² ≈ 0.68). Hit effect sizes (r² 0.00–0.79) sit in the class the power floor permits. All hits should be treated as candidates: visual QC of phenotype levels by genotype and replication in larger placental cohorts come before functional claims.

Three characterization observations:

  1. Modality composition. expression leads the EAS grouped-eGene breakdown (1127 of 2412); expression leads the EUR grouped-eGene breakdown (1298 of 3074) PANTRY’s central finding was that non-expression modalities carry the largest share of regulatory signal; the driver-modality composition of the catalog (above) tests whether that ordering holds in placenta.
  2. Ancestry sharing. 586 of 1379 EAS and 1601 EUR combined-layer eGenes are shared (Fisher OR 7.32, p = 2.5e-195 vs the tested-in-both universe). Shared eGenes are the cross-ancestry replication signal; specific sets are candidates for ancestry-biased regulation.
  3. Functional enrichment. Top g:Profiler term per set: EAS combined eGenes — Metabolic pathways (KEGG, g:SCS p = 9.7e-05); EUR combined eGenes — Metabolic pathways (KEGG, g:SCS p = 0.00034); EUR-specific eGenes — Propanoate metabolism (KEGG, g:SCS p = 0.012); shared eGenes — Metabolic pathways (KEGG, g:SCS p = 0.0018). Full tables in tables/enrichment_*.tsv.

9.1 Literature context

Positive control: the ERAP1/ERAP2 locus (5q15). The strongest signal shared across ancestries is ERAP2 — a top-10 combined-layer gene in both strata (EAS q = 2.4×10⁻¹⁹, expression driver; EUR q = 5.7×10⁻³⁰, isoform-expression driver) — with ERAP1 the #3 gene in EUR (q = 2.4×10⁻²⁹, alt_polyA driver). ERAP2 is a canonical preeclampsia risk locus: fetal-genome variants at ERAP2 associate with preeclampsia in Australian/Norwegian (Johnson et al. 2009), Brazilian (Ferreira et al. 2021), and African American (Hill et al. 2011) cohorts, and ERAP1/ERAP2 are differentially expressed in preeclamptic placentas (Seamon et al. 2020). The EUR driver being isoform expression is mechanism-consistent: the preeclampsia-associated ERAP2 variation tags a haplotype under balancing selection whose molecular effect is alternative splicing and nonsense-mediated decay of ERAP2 transcripts (Andrés et al. 2010; Raja & Kuiper 2023; Ye et al. 2018) — exactly the phenotype class our isoform-expression layer measures. Recovering this locus, through the expected modality, is direct evidence that the atlas captures disease-relevant placental regulation.

Top combined-layer genes, per ancestry. EAS: PGM1 (expression driver) — placental phosphoglucomutase activity is long established (Fazi et al. 1990) and PGM1 loss disrupts cellular energy homeostasis (Conte et al. 2023), relevant to placental glycogen handling in diabetic pregnancy (Lafta et al. 2021); IQCG — ciliary/flagellar function with no prior placental association (novel candidate); PSCA (alt_polyA driver) — overexpressed in gestational trophoblastic neoplasia (Feng et al. 2007); FBLN1 — fibulin-1 functions in placentation (Singh et al. 2006), placental ECM remodeling in late-onset preeclampsia (García-Montero et al. 2026), and maternal plasma fibulin-1 tracking pregnancy progression (Orvik et al. 2021); SPSB2 — an E3-ligase adaptor targeting iNOS for proteasomal degradation (Kuang et al. 2010; Li et al. 2021), placing it in nitric-oxide biology central to placental vascular function. EUR: ZSCAN9 — KRAB zinc-finger with no prior placental association (novel candidate); CTNND1 (RNA-editing driver) — p120-catenin is required for trophoblast proliferation and lineage specification at implantation (Qin et al. 2024) and sits in the Wnt-regulated invasion program (Knöfler & Pollheimer 2013); STBD1 — the glycophagy receptor linking glycogen to selective autophagy (Zhang et al. 2024; Tang et al. 2023), a second glycogen-metabolism hit alongside PGM1.

Sub-threshold top-ranked genes (tables above) remain prioritization hints only — and the flagged low-carrier rows should be discounted outright.

10 Limitations and next steps

  1. Power. n ≈ 280/140 with a ~12k-gene testing burden detects only r² ≳ 0.10 (EAS) / 0.19 (EUR) effects. Doubling n would roughly halve the detectable r²; matching PANTRY’s n = 445 would bring the floor to ≈ 0.06. Adding the remaining cohorts and the AFR/AMR/SAS strata is the highest-value next step.
  2. Carrier-count propagation. The MAC ≥ 5 floor predates outlier exclusion, so low-carrier tests persist in some mapping outputs (audit table above). No reported result depends on them; hit lists should post-filter to ma_count ≥ 5, and re-applying the floor after outlier exclusion would remove them at the source.
  3. Ancestry asymmetry. EUR tests more phenotypes than EAS in every modality (ancestry-specific filtering), so cross-ancestry comparisons are restricted to genes tested in both.
  4. No pooled cross-ancestry inference was performed. If combined discovery is wanted later, Fisher/Stouffer or an inverse-variance slope meta-analysis are the clean options.
  5. Stepwise secondary signals: 585 groups carry a conditionally independent secondary signal (table above).
  6. Fine-mapping and colocalization are out of scope. The natural follow-ups on the FDR-significant catalog are SuSiE fine-mapping per eGene locus, GWAS colocalization (coloc/eCAVIAR) against placental and pregnancy-outcome GWAS, and locus-zoom visual QC of each hit (nominal-scan extraction + LD from the ancestry-matched genotype panel).
  7. Replication path: the FDR-significant hits are the priorities for lookup in larger placental resources or a future meta-analysis; visual QC of phenotype levels by genotype is the immediate sanity check for each.

11 Reproducibility

  • Results: tensorQTL cis mapping (grouped / ungrouped / combined / stepwise), MAF ≥ 0.01 + MAC ≥ 5 at the genotype intersection, ±1 Mb window, Storey q-values on pval_beta via the R qvalue package (singularity-R bridge). Covariates: as described (first-5 PCs + HCP_1–k* + sex/GA/cell types; maternal fraction excluded before correlation pruning; no cap). Genotype PCs: cohort-only plink2 PCA on LD-pruned variants.
  • Pipeline scripts: this repository (05_qtl_mapping/, scripts 19–30 + compute_qvalues.R; genotype pooling in 01_genotype_imputation/).
  • Report code: report_placenta_xqtl.Rmd + xqtl_report_functions.R; figures in figures/, tables in tables/.
  • Gene symbols: gene_map.tsv regenerated in full from the normalized GTF (config normalized_gtf) by make_report_archive.sh at archive time — covers every tested gene, version-stripped IDs.
